correctness.rationale: All 1024 vertex sets were checked by union-find and a separate DFS component criterion; all 785 nonempty simplices, 3470 Hasse incidences and 389 matched pairs checked for an acyclic discrete Morse matching with exactly one critical 0-cell and six critical 5-cells. Thus the integral homotopy type is exactly a wedge of six S^5. Independent GF(2) boundary ranks corroborate homology. Signed simplicial traces on all 120 S5 group elements equal the exterior-square standard-module character; norm one and scalar character uniqueness prove the irreducible Q-module. All steps are rechecked by the executable standalone verifier in this finding.

originality.rationale: The exact vertex-induced forest complex and its complete integral homotopy/S5-module identification are not implied by any inspected primary source, published-result comparison or checked local claim. Closest sources either count acyclic vertex subsets or classify different graph families; analogous Petersen graphic-matroid, cut, independence and Morse complexes have distinct definitions. The overlap checks address equivalences, stronger coverage and the representation coincidence, with explicit residual risks.
residual_risks: Indexing and accessible full-text searches cannot rule out an equivalent calculation in unindexed or inaccessible papers.
An isomorphic six-dimensional S5 representation already appears for the different Petersen three-cut complex; no derived implication was found, but an unpublished conceptual relation is possible.

value.rationale: This gives a complete and natural integral topological classification of the induced acyclic-vertex-set complex of the canonical cubic girth-five Petersen graph, not a contrived finite slice. Its mixed facet dimensions and irreducible S5 homology action are not implied by its decycling number or face enumeration and add an equivariant invariant to an independently motivated graph-complex filtration.
